audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives six of seven stages to Yasuo and Level 6 to 'Skill', while Sejuani wins 55.67% over 203 games and the entry's own prose says 'The moment you hit Level 2 the matchup flips' and 'Sejuani wins the 1v1 convincingly through two items'.
audit.why: The chart says the exact opposite of the paragraphs beside it and of the record. The packet levelChart reads Skill / Sejuani / Sejuani / Sejuani / Sejuani / Sejuani / Yasuo, which matches the kits and the text: Arctic Assault is a dash, so Wind Wall cannot refuse it, and Sweeping Blade cannot re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds, so he needs minions to leave a knock-up. Only at full crit does the duel go back to him.
audit.corrected: Level 1 is even, Levels 2 through the first item belong to Sejuani, and only 2+ items belongs to Yasuo.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (Sweeping Blade: 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds')
champ-data/content/sejuani.js (early and late paragraphs of this entry)

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in six places across both layers and its duration and cooldown never appear once. Last Breath is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: The plan the entry sells is 'bait the wall, then throw R'. That plan needs two numbers it does not have: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17 seconds and stands for 4. Knowing it is a four-second wall on a twenty-five second cooldown is what turns 'wait for it to expire' into a count you can actually run. Last Breath is 70/50/30 — the shortest ultimate cooldown in the matchup by a wide margin and, at rank 3, up more often than Sejuani's Arctic Assault.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (Wind Wall cd 25/23/21/19/17, 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds'; Last Breath cd 70/50/30)

audit.whatIsWrong: Last Breath can only be cast on an Airborne enemy champion. Arctic Assault knocks enemies into the air. Neither layer mentions that Sejuani's own engage is what arms Yasuo's ultimate.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it is the one thing that can turn a winning lane into a lost fight. Riot's text is explicit: Last Breath 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion'. From level 6 onward, every Arctic Assault Sejuani throws at Yasuo hands him the trigger for a 70-second ultimate that also holds her in the air. The entry currently teaches the player to open every fight with Q — correct before 6, and a coin flip after it, unless he knows to check whether Last Breath is up first. The mirror rule also applies from his side of the page: his engage is her engage.
audit.corrected: Your Arctic Assault knock-up is Airborne, and Last Breath only fires on an Airborne target — from 6, check whether his R is up before you Q him, or open with Permafrost instead.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (Last Breath: 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion ... holding all Airborne enemies in the area in the air')
champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (Arctic Assault: 'charges forward, knocking enemies into the air')

audit.whatIsWrong: Way of the Wanderer builds a shield whenever Yasuo is moving and triggers on the first champion damage he takes. Neither layer mentions it.
audit.why: It is the reason the first Winter's Wrath arc of a trade reliably does nothing. A Sejuani opening the Frost-stack pattern on a Yasuo who has been walking the lane spends her opener stripping a shield rather than building toward Permafrost, which shifts the whole trade one arc later than the entry's timing assumes. Chip it off with an auto before committing the combo and the sequencing the entry describes actually works.
audit.corrected: Way of the Wanderer shields him whenever he has been moving — pop it with an auto before you commit, or your first Winter's Wrath arc is spent on the shield instead of on Frost.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (Way of the Wanderer: 'builds toward a shield whenever he is moving. The shield triggers when he takes damage from a champion')

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says 'let your passive Permafrost armor stack' and 'Stack Permafrost passive resistances between trades' — Permafrost is Sejuani's E stun and has no passive, and Frost Armor does not stack.
audit.why: Frost Armor is a single out-of-combat buff, not something that accumulates over repeated trades, so 'stack it between trades' describes a mechanic that does not exist. Worse, it hides the condition that does exist: staying out of combat. Against a Steel Tempest poking every 4 seconds, understanding that any chip resets the buff is the whole reason to hold the tip of the wave.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor from Fury of the North is a single buff gained out of combat and lost shortly after damage — it does not stack, and his Steel Tempest chip is what keeps it off.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (Fury of the North; Permafrost descriptions)

edits.after: Q knocks him Airborne, both Winter's Wrath arcs stack Frost, then Permafrost stuns before Sweeping Blade finds a minion — his E cannot re-target you for a few seconds.

edits.after: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 and stands for 4 seconds — engage with Q so he burns it, then throw Glacial Prison, which the wall would otherwise eat whole as a projectile.

edits.before: Two crit items and Yasuo dashes through your CC windows faster than you can reset them — peel for your carries rather than hunting him solo.
edits.after: Your Q knock-up is what arms Last Breath — 70/50/30s, Airborne targets only. Check his R before you charge, or open with Permafrost.

edits.before: Stack Permafrost passive resistances between trades so every all-in he takes punishes him more than you
edits.after: Let Frost Armor rebuild out of combat between trades so every all-in he takes costs him more than you

edits.before: Deploy Windwall to block your Glacial Prison before you can engage from range
edits.after: Ride your own Arctic Assault knock-up into Last Breath, or Wind Wall your R

edits.before: Both kits are weak at Level 1 — take W, last-hit, and let Permafrost passive stack resistances between his Q tornados.
edits.after: Both kits are weak at Level 1 — take W, last-hit, and let Frost Armor rebuild between Steel Tempest prods, out of combat.

edits.before: Your Q charge is a dash, not a projectile — Windwall does not stop it, and Yasuo has no escape from a Level 2 knockup.
edits.after: Your Q is a dash, so Wind Wall cannot refuse it — but the knock-up is Airborne, and that is what Last Breath needs.

edits.before: From Levels 4-6 your primary job is Windwall management: never throw R first into an upright Windwall. Instead, open every fight with Q charge — the dash cannot be blocked — then force the wall with a fake R throw or a traded ability, and only commit Glacial Prison once it is down or expired. At Level 6 a Q-engage into a jungle gank is a near-guaranteed kill; your R's blizzard zone slows everyone inside so even a wall-blocked throw gives your jungler free CC. Yasuo needs to burn his Windwall defensively in this window or it is wasted as an offensive tool.
edits.after: From Levels 4-6 your primary job is Wind Wall management: never throw R first into an upright wall — it is a projectile and the wall eats it whole. Open every fight with Q charge, which is a dash and cannot be blocked, force the wall out, count 25 seconds at rank 1, and only then commit Glacial Prison. From 6 add one check before you charge: your Q knock-up is Airborne, and Last Breath only fires on an Airborne target, so a Q into an available ultimate hands him the fight. If his R is up, open with Permafrost and keep the charge for the exit.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your Q dash like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Yasuo Wind Wall: 25/23/21/19/17s, standing 4 seconds — it eats Glacial Prison whole, so hold R until it is spent. - Last Breath: 70/50/30s, and only on an Airborne target — your own Q arms it. - Guard your Q.

notes: Best find: Last Breath only fires on an Airborne enemy champion, and Arctic Assault knocks enemies into the air. From level 6 the entry's core instruction — 'open every fight with Q charge' — is the exact input Yasuo's ultimate needs, and neither layer mentions it anywhere. The fix is one check before the charge, not a change of plan. Second: Way of the Wanderer builds a shield whenever he is moving, so the first Winter's Wrath arc of a trade is routinely spent stripping it rather than stacking Frost; that shifts the whole combo timing one arc later than the entry assumes. Third: Wind Wall is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in six places across both layers and neither its 25/23/21/19/17s cooldown nor its 4-second duration appears once, which makes 'wait for it to expire' a count with no numbers. NOTE ON THE PACKET DEFECT: it reports the entry 'never names any of Yasuo's abilities'. That is a detector artefact — the entry writes 'Windwall' as one word throughout, which the matcher misses. I have standardised the instances I touched to Riot's 'Wind Wall'; the applier should sweep the remainder.
